title: I created a whole shared ecosystem of blob creatures which you, the gods can corrupt. Its probably more an experiment than a game though.
author: Tom_Baron
selftext:
The idea came to me in severe sleep disruption caused by my 3 year old and is completely ridiculous.

Pic is an early world where mutations are making subtle changes to the blobs appearance, I don't want to give the game away!

https://i.redd.it/vc6ou4y2il1i1.png

A shared world of blobs. Starting as "perfect" grey creatures on an island of abundant resources. They eat, love, fight and die. Forming societies, dynasties and being enlightened to religion along the way.

The problem is the humans! Everyone can interact via voting and emojing(?) The interactions the blobs have modifying the blobs learnt experience. Every 30 minutes real news (via rss feed, bad stuff filtered out) lands into the game and this is turned into a DNA mutation, morphing them in appearance, ability and behaviour which the players vote on to apply to the blobs. You speak via their religions to them to influence their behaviour and cast blessings or curses on their world every game night.

The tech is system one models managing all interactions and mutation creating, its all browser based, WebGPU/three.js   


And things get really wild as time goes on! Note the emergence of the big hats in this early world, that's just a tiny sign of things to come. 

I've been engrossed in their lives alongside my colleagues for a full dev "season" so far, seeing a dominant society rise through a great blob war, religions came and passed, world leaders emerged and their bloodlines died out, ancestors of founding blobs avenging the deaths of their relatives. I restarted today for another baseline test.

Its completely wild and I have no idea what to do with it. It'll handle 200 "players" on a render instance though. There are 100s of hours left of dev time to iron out all the wrinkles and the small matter of sound first though!

  
I do wonder if there is there a market out there for SUPER idle sim/games or have I just created a fun experiment? I'm happy with either really!
